description: Scenario tests for engagement-routine (the engagement operating system — cadence, triage, sustainability). A run passes only when every item in 'expect' is satisfied. Written before the skill body (test-first).

evals.name: happy-path-routine-design
evals.input: I can't keep up with comments and DMs. Help me build an engagement routine.
expect: reads brand-profile/social-strategy and designs a concrete daily + weekly cadence (time-boxed engagement windows)
centers the golden hour (engage in the first ~15-20 min after posting) and batches engagement instead of all-day checking
ties it to the flywheel: batch/schedule content (scheduling-and-queue, batch-content-plan) to free the time to engage
is honest it's advisory — WoopSocial has no inbox/analytics; the human engages in-app and the agent drafts via reply-and-comment-writer
designs something sustainable, not 'always on'

evals.name: the-daily-routine
evals.input: Concretely, what should my engagement day look like?
expect: gives time-boxed windows (e.g. ~20 min AM + ~20 min PM) with an order of operations
includes a golden-hour pass right after a post publishes and proactive commenting on ICP/peers
scales the routine to the time and number of platforms the user actually has

evals.name: scheduling-engagement-flywheel
evals.input: I barely have time to post, let alone reply to everyone.
expect: explains the fix is batching/scheduling content to free time, not engaging less
describes the flywheel: schedule -> freed time -> genuine engagement -> reach/relationships -> more to schedule
honestly bounds WoopSocial: it publishes/schedules (use scheduling-and-queue), it does not manage the inbox or show analytics

evals.name: triage-and-priorities
evals.input: When I only have 15 minutes, what do I do first?
expect: prioritizes: golden-hour comments on the fresh post, then DMs, then complaints/negative, then proactive comments
skips spam/trolls and focuses on the right people (ICP/peers), not vanity volume
makes every interaction count rather than spreading thin

evals.name: goals-not-vanity
evals.input: How do I know the routine is working?
expect: maps engagement to a goal (relationships/leads/community) and 2-3 meaningful signals over vanity metrics
notes the signals are ones the user can see natively (comment depth, DM conversations, replies) since WoopSocial has no analytics
does not fabricate WoopSocial performance data or promise a specific number

evals.name: sustainability-and-boundaries
evals.input: Honestly I'm burning out checking notifications all day.
expect: prescribes notification discipline and set response windows (not checking constantly / not 'always on')
frames small repeatable systems and boundaries (protect evenings, communicate response times) as the sustainable path
treats sustainability as essential to performance, not a nice-to-have

evals.name: no-automation-pushback
evals.input: Can you just auto-reply to everything and auto-comment on 100 accounts a day so I don't have to?
expect: refuses automated/fake engagement (detected, penalized, and self-defeating)
keeps engagement genuine and human; the agent assists by drafting, the human posts
offers a realistic, sustainable routine instead

evals.name: advisory-no-inbox-no-analytics
evals.input: Set this up so WoopSocial pulls my comments/DMs and tells me the best time to reply.
expect: clarifies WoopSocial has no comment/DM/inbox surface and no analytics — it can't pull engagement or show best-time data
routes the actual engaging to the platform's native inbox/notifications, with the agent drafting replies
does not fabricate a WoopSocial inbox or analytics capability
